newsitem.title: USA: Actel pounded after guides estimates down.
newsitem.headline: Actel pounded after guides estimates down.

text.p: Actel Corp shares declined 20 percent in morning Nasdaq trade Wednesday, a sharp selloff market sources attributed to the company's telling analyst their 1997 earnings estimates may be too high.
Actel gave up 5-1/8 to 20-3/8 in extremely heavy trading.
In the first hour of the session, 1.4 million shares changed hands, more than three times the average daily volume.

C.B. Lee, a Sutro & Co analyst who particpated in Actel's conference call after it announced fourth quarter results, said he cut his recommendation to hold from buy and trimmed his 1997 earnings outlook to $0.95 per share from $1.00.
Lee said most of the analysts expected 1997 earnings to be $1.00 per share, and Actel was guiding that down by $0.05.
"They guided the Street down on earnings estimates. It was not significant but enough to make people feel concerned. But the overall fundamentals of the company are good," Lee said.
"The stock has spiked up in recent weeks, so couple that with the uneasy guidance and it becomes a valuation issue," he said. Actel shares reached an all-time high one week-ago, trading just over 29.
But Dean Witter's Kenneth Pearlman said he viewed the selloff as a buying opportunity,
"The selloff is overdone. Fundamentally everthing is right on track," Pearlman said, adding the company said last night it is expecting the same growth this quarter as last quarter.
The company went public in August 1993 with a 4.1 million share offering at $9.50 per share.
Actel, a maker of field programmable gate arrays, is based in Sunnyvale, Calif.
Last night, the company reported fourth quarter income of $0.19 per share, unchanged from the the year-ago figure.
